title: The Automated QBR (Quarterly Business Review)
tagline: Build the quarterly business review from data, not from a weekend of slides: quarter-over-quarter results vs goals, wins and risks picked by rule, chart SVGs, a slide outline, and an ROI model with a conservative case.
why: A QBR is the moment a customer decides whether to renew and expand. Most CSMs spend a day per account copying numbers into slides, and the ROI claim is often a guess the customer's CFO ignores. An automated QBR pulls the same metrics every quarter, applies the same rules for what counts as a win or a risk, and shows ROI with a conservative case the CFO can trust.
covers: Quarter-over-quarter change per metric, with direction (higher or lower is better) and goal met / missed
Rule-based wins (met goal or improved ≥ threshold) and risks (missed goal and declined); status on_track / improving / at_risk
Bar-chart SVG per metric (last Q, this Q, dashed goal line), text escaped
Slide outline in a fixed order: title, results vs goals, wins, value delivered, risks and asks, next quarter
ROI model: time saved × loaded rate, revenue lift × gross margin, cost avoided; ROI %, net, payback months; base and conservative (haircut) cases
gaps: Outputs an outline and SVGs, not a .pptx or Google Slides file
No CRM / product-analytics pull: metrics are synthetic JSON
No narrative LLM writing: bullets are deterministic
